Subject: internal: cost assumptions + sensitivity table for ACME MAP

Internal note — replying here to capture technical assumptions I used so we can update the MAP: see bullets below (I’ll paste into the spreadsheet later).

- Model: rdx-7b-q4f (approx numbers for hosted): compute per-token = 0.00085 USD/token (in our public hosted price model); optimized Dedicated pricing reduces compute by ~35% at high utilization.
- Prefix (KV) caching: I used TTL=12h for Optimistic scenario; with doc updates daily the effective hit-rate for doc-QA is ~65-72% if we do prefix-level caching (we cache doc vectors + prefix tokens). Conservative case uses TTL=2h -> hit-rate ~35-45%.
- Batching: assumed average batch size depends on concurrency. For PoC traffic we modeled a baseline of avg batch=4 (p95 concurrency fit), optimistic batch=8 (clients buffer), conservative batch=2 (real-time single-shot). Per-request overhead (network + decoding start) ~6ms; batching reduces per-token overhead but adds tail-latency risk.
- Cost sensitivity: 10% change in hit-rate gives ~7% change in token bill for doc-QA heavy workloads; batching shifts unit cost more when avg prompt size is small (i.e., for the alert generation flow, batching is critical).

Open items for spreadsheet: explicit mapping of your expected 48-hr trace to hit-rate buckets and an eval run that simulates caching with document churn of 1x/day.
